question: Which of following silver coins was introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tanka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish (of the Delhi Sultanate's Slave/Mamluk dynasty) introduced the silver "Tanka" and the copper "Jital", laying the basis of the Sultanate's coinage system. (चाँदी का टंका — इल्तुतमिश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The silver tanka later became the standard silver coin, and the rupee of the Mughals evolved from this tradition.

• Iltutmish (r. 1211–1236) was the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate; he completed the Qutub Minar and set up the Iqta system.

NOTE

• Iltutmish also organised the "Chahalgani/Chalisa" — a group of forty powerful Turkish nobles. His coins bore his name and titles in Arabic.

question: Wasifuddin Dagar was associated with which of the following classical music genres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhrupad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Wasifuddin Dagar is a renowned exponent of "Dhrupad", one of the oldest forms of Hindustani classical vocal music. He belongs to the celebrated Dagar family (Dagarvani gharana). (ध्रुपद — वासिफुद्दीन डागर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dhrupad is a solemn, devotional and highly structured style, older than Khyal; it emphasises the pure elaboration of the raga (alap) and rhythmic patterns.

• The Dagar family has preserved the Dhrupad tradition for many generations.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal styles: Dhrupad, Khyal, Thumri, Tarana and Ghazal. Dhrupad is considered the most ancient and austere among them.

question: When was the Lahore declaration signed between India and Pakistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is February 1999.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Lahore Declaration" was signed between India and Pakistan in February 1999 (on 21 February 1999), by Prime Ministers Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Nawaz Sharif. (लाहौर घोषणा — फरवरी 1999)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It followed Vajpayee's historic Delhi–Lahore bus journey and aimed at reducing the risk of nuclear conflict and improving bilateral ties.

• The spirit of the declaration was soon undermined by the Kargil War (May–July 1999).

NOTE

• Key India–Pakistan agreements: Tashkent Agreement (1966), Shimla Agreement (1972) and Lahore Declaration (1999).

question: According to Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022, what was the population of the poor in India in 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 228.9 million.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2022 (released by UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative, OPHI), the number of multidimensionally poor people in India in 2020 was about 228.9 million. (बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2022)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The MPI measures poverty across three dimensions — health, education and standard of living — using ten indicators.

• The report noted that India had significantly reduced its poverty over the years.

NOTE

• India also publishes its own National MPI through NITI Aayog, aligned with the global methodology, tracking deprivations in health, education and living standards.

question: The part of a temple wherein the main deity of the temple is housed is known as the _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Garbha Griha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Garbha Griha" (literally the "womb chamber") is the innermost sanctum of a Hindu temple where the main deity (idol) is housed. (गर्भगृह — मुख्य देवता का स्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shikhara — the towering spire built above the garbha griha (in North Indian/Nagara temples).

• Mandapa — the pillared hall in front of the sanctum where devotees gather.

• Stupa — a Buddhist dome-shaped structure containing relics (not a part of a Hindu temple).

NOTE

• Temple architecture styles in India: Nagara (North), Dravida (South, with a gopuram gateway and vimana tower) and Vesara (a blend of both).

question: Sama Chakeva is a folk dance based on the mythological story of the siblings Sama and Chakeva, in which the brother goes to an extreme extent to save his sister. With which State of India is this folk dance associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sama Chakeva" is a traditional folk dance/festival of the Mithila region of Bihar (also popular in parts of Nepal and Jharkhand). It celebrates the bond between brother and sister through the mythological story of Sama and Chakeva. (सामा-चकेवा — बिहार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It is celebrated mainly by women during the Kartik month (November) and involves making clay figures of birds and singing folk songs.

• It reflects the theme of sibling love, similar in spirit to Raksha Bandhan and Bhai Dooj.

NOTE

• Folk dances of Bihar: Jat-Jatin, Sama Chakeva, Jhijhian, Bidesia and Paika.

question: Which of the following is an autobiography of LK Advani?
solution_text:
The correct answer is My Country My Life.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "My Country My Life" is the autobiography of veteran politician and former Deputy Prime Minister Lal Krishna Advani (L. K. Advani), published in 2008. (माई कंट्री माई लाइफ — एल. के. आडवाणी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Exam Warriors — written by Narendra Modi.

• Wings of Fire — autobiography of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

• Dare to Dream — a biography associated with Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam / on his life and ideas.

NOTE

• L. K. Advani was a founder-leader of the BJP, led the Ram Rath Yatra (1990), and served as Home Minister and Deputy PM in the Vajpayee government. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna (2024).

question: The 'Rule of Law' is a key feature of the Indian Constitution which is a doctrine ascribed to ____________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Albert Venn Dicey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The doctrine of the "Rule of Law" is ascribed to the British jurist Albert Venn Dicey (A. V. Dicey), who expounded it in his book "Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution (1885)". (विधि का शासन — ए. वी. डायसी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dicey identified three elements of the Rule of Law: (i) supremacy of law, (ii) equality before the law, and (iii) the predominance of the legal spirit (rights coming from judicial decisions).

• The concept is enshrined in the Indian Constitution mainly through Article 14 (equality before law and equal protection of laws).

NOTE

• The Rule of Law is part of the basic structure of the Constitution and ensures that no one is above the law and that the government itself is bound by law.

question: Who among the following Governor Generals of India wrote about the predicament of Indian weavers, “The bones of the cotton weavers are scattered on the plains of India”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord William Bentinck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord William Bentinck (Governor-General, 1828–1835) famously remarked on the ruin of Indian handloom weavers: "The bones of the cotton weavers are bleaching the plains of India", describing the devastation caused by cheap British machine-made cloth. (लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bentinck introduced major social reforms — the abolition of Sati (1829) with Raja Ram Mohan Roy's support, and the suppression of Thuggee.

• On Macaulay's recommendation, he promoted English education in India (1835).

NOTE

• Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India (under the Charter Act of 1833); earlier the post was Governor-General of Bengal.

question: The Dudhsagar waterfall is a major tourist place of ________ State.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Dudhsagar Waterfall" (meaning "sea of milk") is a major tourist attraction located on the Mandovi River in the state of Goa, on the Goa–Karnataka border in the Western Ghats. (दूधसागर जलप्रपात — गोवा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is one of India's tallest waterfalls (about 310 m) and lies within the Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary and Mollem National Park.

• The falls appear as a cascade of white foamy water resembling milk, hence the name.

NOTE

• Other famous waterfalls of India: Kunchikal (Karnataka), Jog Falls (Karnataka), Nohkalikai (Meghalaya), Athirappilly (Kerala).

question: Who became the first woman to win two gold medals in a single Para Asian Games event in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sheetal Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sheetal Devi, the para-archer from Jammu and Kashmir, became the first woman to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games (Hangzhou, 2023). (शीतल देवी — पैरा तीरंदाज़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sheetal Devi, born with phocomelia (undeveloped arms), shoots the bow using her legs and feet, and is one of the world's few armless archers competing internationally.

• She won golds in the women's individual compound and mixed team compound events.

NOTE

• Sheetal Devi is a rising icon of Indian para-sport and was later honoured with the Arjuna Award.

question: In the periodic table, what is the trend for atomic radius as you move from left to right across a period (horizontal row)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atomic radius decreases.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As we move from left to right across a period, the atomic radius decreases. This is because the nuclear charge (number of protons) increases while electrons are added to the same shell, so the nucleus pulls the electrons in more strongly. (परमाणु त्रिज्या घटती है)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Down a group, the atomic radius increases because new electron shells are added, increasing the distance of the outermost electrons from the nucleus.

• Trends across a period: atomic radius decreases, ionisation energy increases, electronegativity increases, metallic character decreases.

NOTE

• The modern periodic law (Henry Moseley) states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.

question: Gulabo Sapera, a legendry folk dancer from Kalbeliya tribe, Rajasthan, received Padma Shri in the year ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gulabo Sapera, the celebrated Kalbeliya dancer from Rajasthan, was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016 for her contribution to art. (गुलाबो सपेरा — पद्म श्री 2016)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Kalbeliya dance, performed by the Kalbeliya (snake-charmer) community, was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• The graceful, serpent-like movements of the dancers give the dance its distinctive character.

NOTE

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India, after the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan.

question: Which of the following white papers, released by NITI Aayog, is related to Public Health Surveillance in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vision 2035.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vision 2035: Public Health Surveillance in India" is the white paper released by NITI Aayog that lays out a roadmap to strengthen India's public health surveillance system. (विज़न 2035 — नीति आयोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It aims to make India's surveillance system responsive and predictive, integrating it with the Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres and using data and technology.

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in 2015; its chairperson is the Prime Minister.

NOTE

• Public health surveillance became especially important after the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the need for early detection and rapid response systems.

question: Who amongst the following said that the government fiscal policy should be used to stabilise the level of output and employment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is JM Keynes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• John Maynard Keynes (J. M. Keynes) argued that the government's fiscal policy (taxation and public spending) should be used to stabilise the level of output and employment, especially during depressions. (जे. एम. कीन्स — राजकोषीय नीति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Keynes's famous work is "The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money (1936)", written after the Great Depression of 1929.

• He is regarded as the father of modern macroeconomics and advocated government intervention to boost demand.

NOTE

• Adam Smith — father of economics ("Wealth of Nations"); Alfred Marshall — "Principles of Economics"; Lionel Robbins — famous scarcity definition of economics.

question: Which of the following options is an example of a decomposer in an ecosystem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fungus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Fungus" is a decomposer — it breaks down dead plants and animals and returns nutrients to the soil. (कवक — अपघटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Decomposers (e.g., fungi and bacteria) are called saprotrophs; they recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem.

• Producers (green plants) make food by photosynthesis; herbivores eat plants; carnivores eat other animals.

NOTE

• Ecosystem components: Producers → Primary consumers (herbivores) → Secondary/Tertiary consumers (carnivores) → Decomposers. Decomposers complete the nutrient cycle.

question: Who among the following social reformers wrote Brahmo Covenant which was a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Debendranath Tagore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Debendranath Tagore wrote the "Brahmo Covenant (Brahmo Dharma)", a statement of the creed/principles of the Brahmo Samaj. He reorganised and revitalised the Samaj after Raja Ram Mohan Roy. (देवेंद्रनाथ टैगोर — ब्रह्म समाज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 (as Brahmo Sabha); Debendranath Tagore joined it and later led it, founding the Tattvabodhini Sabha.

• Debendranath Tagore was the father of the poet Rabindranath Tagore.

• Keshab Chandra Sen later led a more radical faction of the Brahmo Samaj.

NOTE

• The Brahmo Samaj opposed idol worship, the caste system and social evils like Sati, and promoted monotheism and social reform.

question: In which of the following states is the famous International Sand Art Festival organised, where artists get enthralled by the diverse thoughts and their elucidation on sand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous "International Sand Art Festival" is organised annually at Chandrabhaga Beach, Konark, in Odisha. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सैंड आर्ट फेस्टिवल — ओडिशा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is held alongside the Konark Festival in December, attracting sand artists from India and abroad.

• Odisha's Sudarsan Pattnaik is a world-renowned sand artist who has won many international awards.

NOTE

• Odisha's cultural landmarks: the Sun Temple at Konark (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), the Jagannath Temple at Puri, and the Odissi classical dance.

question: Which sector uses the groundwater maximally?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Agriculture" sector uses groundwater maximally in India — most of the extracted groundwater is used for irrigation. (कृषि क्षेत्र — भूजल का सर्वाधिक उपयोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India is the largest user of groundwater in the world; agriculture accounts for roughly 80–90% of groundwater use.

• Over-extraction (especially through tube wells) has led to falling water tables in states like Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

NOTE

• The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) monitors and manages groundwater; schemes like Atal Bhujal Yojana promote sustainable groundwater management.

question: The black coating formed on silver jewellery is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ag2S.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The black coating on silver articles/jewellery is silver sulphide (Ag₂S). It forms when silver reacts with hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) present in air (tarnishing/corrosion of silver). (सिल्वर सल्फाइड — Ag₂S)

◦ Reaction: 2Ag + H₂S → Ag₂S + H₂.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Similarly, copper develops a green coating of basic copper carbonate, and iron forms rust (hydrated iron oxide).

• Silver ornaments are cleaned to remove this black tarnish and restore shine.

NOTE

• Common compounds: AgNO₃ (silver nitrate, used in photography), AgCl (silver chloride), Ag₂CO₃ (silver carbonate). Only Ag₂S is the black tarnish on silver.

question: The Megalithic site __________ is a site on the river Ghod, a tributary of the Bhima.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Inamgaon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inamgaon" is an archaeological (Chalcolithic/megalithic) site located on the banks of the Ghod River, a tributary of the Bhima River, in Maharashtra. (इनामगाँव — घोड नदी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Inamgaon was a major settlement of the Jorwe culture (a Chalcolithic culture of the Deccan) and gives evidence of farming, houses, and burial practices.

• The people practised agriculture and animal domestication and used black-and-red ware pottery.

NOTE

• Other important prehistoric/megalithic sites: Hire Benakal, Hallur (Karnataka) and Brahmagiri; Inamgaon is a key site for understanding Deccan Chalcolithic life.

question: Which of the following crops takes almost a year to grow?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sugarcane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sugarcane" is a long-duration crop that takes almost a year (about 10–18 months) to mature. (गन्ना — लगभग एक वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sugarcane is a tropical/subtropical, Kharif-season crop needing hot, humid climate and plenty of water; Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are leading producers.

• It is the main source of sugar, gur (jaggery) and khandsari, and the byproduct bagasse is used for making paper and generating power.

NOTE

• Short-duration crops like ragi, soybean and groundnut mature in a few months; sugarcane is distinct for its long growing period.

question: The strength of Supreme Court has increased to how many judges as of 13 Feb 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 34.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of 13 February 2023, the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court of India stood at 34 judges — that is, 1 Chief Justice of India + 33 other judges. (उच्चतम न्यायालय — 34 न्यायाधीश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The strength was raised from 31 to 34 by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019.

• Article 124 of the Constitution provides for the establishment of the Supreme Court; Parliament can fix the number of judges by law.

NOTE

• Supreme Court judges hold office until the age of 65 years; High Court judges retire at 62 years.

question: Which state received the Sportstar ACES Best State for the Promotion of Sport award in 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tamil Nadu received the "Sportstar ACES Best State for the Promotion of Sport" award in 2024, recognising its efforts in developing sports infrastructure and talent. (तमिलनाडु — 2024)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Sportstar ACES Awards are presented by Sportstar magazine (of The Hindu Group) to honour India's top athletes and sporting achievements.

• Tamil Nadu has actively promoted sport through its state sports policy and events like the Khelo India initiatives.

NOTE

• Khelo India and the National Sports Awards (Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award) are key platforms for promoting sports in India.

question: The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists, which are the Union List, the State List and the _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Concurrent List.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution: the Union List, the State List and the Concurrent List. (समवर्ती सूची — Concurrent List)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Union List — subjects on which only Parliament can legislate (e.g., defence, foreign affairs, currency).

• State List — subjects for State legislatures (e.g., police, public health, agriculture).

• Concurrent List — subjects on which both Centre and States can legislate (e.g., education, marriage, forests); in case of conflict, central law prevails.

NOTE

• This three-fold division is given in the Seventh Schedule (Article 246); the scheme was borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935. Residuary powers rest with the Union.
